clue.text: Condition of brain damage, having dropped an ecstasy inside twice

indicators.note: twice says the assembled piece is written out a second time
having dropped says a letter is let fall into the middle of what remains
inside confirms the drug letter goes within the shortened word
damage here means harm done to the word brain by knocking letters out of it

parts.note: E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A medical note about a patient whose brain was harmed after taking ecstasy pills more than once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' removes A and N from BRAIN, leaving BRI; E goes inside to make BERI, and 'twice' doubles it. The removed letters are not adjacent.
explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is a disease caused by thiamine deficiency, so it is a medical condition.

clue.text: Tense withdrawing record label's money commercially?

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: withdrawing means drawing back, so the label's name is read from right to left

parts.note: EMI is a well-known British record label

explanation.surface: A record company pulls out of a deal over money, and nerves are frayed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'time is money', true above all in business. This is also a Pink Floyd track on the themed album.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says that in business hours spent are as valuable as cash, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Setting one story about head of Man United — on the contrary

indicators.note: about would normally put the first pieces round the later one
on the contrary flips the stated container relation, so the later pieces go round the earlier ones
head of picks the opening letter of the word Man

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for United in team names
I is the Roman numeral for one
a story can be a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: A tale about the boss of Manchester United, told the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'one story about head of Man United' would put ILIE round M; 'on the contrary' reverses that, so M and U go round ILIE. Man United is the football club Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is someone's social surroundings or environment, the setting they live in.

clue.text: Took as hidden theme for work — an album, right?

indicators.note: work as a verb means to knead or shape, so these words are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician hid a recurring motif in a composition and asks if the record works.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Pink Floyd's 1973 album, the puzzle's theme: its track titles are scattered through the clues, and 'right?' hints that the band's name runs down the grid's right-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the best-selling 1973 LP by the British rock band Pink Floyd.

clue.text: Enquire about health of art — fake's criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word fake with its 's read as an S

explanation.surface: A dealer laments that an art forgery is a crime against the work's good name.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask after someone is to inquire how they are, especially their wellbeing.

clue.text: Unbreakable '80s artist that is covering number

parts.note: Adam Ant was a British pop star of the early 1980s

indicators.note: covering means the abbreviation wraps round the number letter

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A tribute to a 1980s pop act whose song cannot be broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamantine describes something as hard as diamond, impossible to break.

clue.text: Actor drawing in John?

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, as is bog
a drawing is a piece of art

explanation.surface: A performer sketching a man named John.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name; it is slang for the toilet, so a drawing in the john is BOG ART, Humphrey Bogart.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Bogart was the Hollywood star of Casablanca and The Maltese Falcon.

clue.text: Atrocious shield ivy cut off

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone wrong signals that the letters are disordered
cut means the word ivy is trimmed of its last letter

explanation.surface: A gardener's complaint that ivy hacked away from a protective shield has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims IVY to IV; SHIELD plus IV is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish can mean extremely bad, fiendish, which matches atrocious.

clue.text: See 4
Eclipse fell

definitions.meaning: to eclipse something is to obscure or conceal it from view
a fell is an animal's skin or pelt

explanation.definitionFit: To hide is to obscure, as an eclipse does; a hide is also a pelt, as fell means.

clue.text: Takeaway, say, at home — order main from specials board?

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: from specials is read loosely as being placed within the next word, the setter's own looser container signal

parts.note: deal is timber, planks of pine or fir board

indicators.note: order as a verb means to arrange, so the word main is rearranged

explanation.surface: Ordering a takeaway at home, picking the main course from the specials board.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter admitted that reading 'from' as a container signal is a little naughty; the order of the main course only makes sense as wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A takeaway, such as a curry, is a typical example of a meal from an Indian restaurant.

clue.text: Having an unoriginal experience for all to see — against a Jedi's short return

indicators.note: return means come back, so the whole string is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all
V is short for versus, against

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A Star Wars fan faces a Jedi's brief comeback in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims JEDI to JED; U, V, A and JED together are then turned round to give DEJAVU.
explanation.definitionFit: Deja vu is the eerie feeling of having lived through the present moment before, so nothing feels new.

clue.text: Starting argument — applying oneself to getting Jordan-like breast augmentation?

indicators.note: Jordan, the British glamour model Katie Price, had implants taking her cup size up, so the DD becomes a larger GG

parts.note: to address a task is to apply oneself to it

explanation.surface: A tabloid quip about someone fixated on surgery to imitate a glamour model.
explanation.walkthrough: Jordan was the stage name of Katie Price, a British glamour model famous for breast implants. Swapping the DD cup in ADDRESSING for a bigger GG gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggressing means making an attack or starting a quarrel first.

clue.text: Shocking riot outside, English fan restrained

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters go round the other pieces
shocking suggests something thrown into disorder, so riot is rearranged

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fan, as in a health nut

explanation.surface: A dreadful riot breaks out but one English supporter holds back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fan' looks like a football supporter at a riot; it is the slang sense of an enthusiast. The answer is an Italian musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritenuto is a musical direction meaning held back, slowing at once.

clue.text: AC/DC left set of great gig — in Sky, high definition's quite extensive

parts.note: AC/DC is slang for bisexual, shortened to bi

indicators.note: the left-hand letters of a run of words are their initials

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for high, as on pencils or taps

explanation.surface: A rock band review: a great gig, broadcast on Sky in high definition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'AC/DC' looks like the rock band; it is slang for bisexual. 'definition's' tells the solver that what follows is the definition. The Great Gig in the Sky is a track on the themed album.
explanation.definitionFit: Biggish means fairly large, so quite extensive in size or scope.

clue.text: Eskimo rolls in way where it's most difficult to breathe?

definitions.text: where it's most difficult to breathe?

indicators.note: rolls means tumbles over, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: An Inuit paddler turning a kayak in a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: An Eskimo roll is a kayaking move, which disguises 'rolls' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The air that is fullest of fumes is hardest to breathe, a cryptic view of a superlative.

clue.text: Bird in paper with unknown weakness

indicators.note: in places the bird within the newspaper's initials

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
a rail is a wading bird
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A bird appears in the newspaper alongside a mysterious weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: Frailty means a weakness of body or character.

clue.text: Score recorders almost speak to me in resurrecting New York line

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: to speak is to talk

indicators.note: in puts the pronoun within the reversed pieces
resurrecting means raising up, which in a down entry turns the letters backwards

explanation.surface: A plea to talk to someone about bringing back a New York railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'resurrecting' (raising up) reads the letters bottom to top, giving LYN; a tallyman was also a door-to-door collector of credit payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallymen keep a tally, recording counts or debts collected, so they record scores.

clue.text: See 4
Live helium light attracts this beast

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
He is the chemical symbol for helium
a moth is the insect drawn to a lamp

explanation.surface: A helium lamp is so bright it draws a huge creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A behemoth is a huge beast, from the Book of Job.

clue.text: Set of nine regularly weaning elands

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of these words

explanation.surface: Nine young antelopes being weaned on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: An ennead is a group of nine, from the Greek for nine.

clue.text: Ancient internet provider, say, recalled within Germany

indicators.note: within puts the reversed pair inside the provider's name

parts.note: AOL is the American internet service provider

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: An old internet company recalls something in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Age-old means having existed for a very long time, so ancient.

clue.text: A second on the run, ultimately like that time

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of the word run

explanation.surface: Someone a second ahead while fleeing, like before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time', a Pink Floyd track, appears here as part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As then means in the way things were at that past moment.

clue.text: Lens corrects against back of prism at …

indicators.note: corrects means puts right, so these letters are rearranged
back of picks the last letter of the word prism

explanation.surface: An optician's lens that fixes problems with a prism.
explanation.definitionFit: An anastigmat is a lens corrected for astigmatism.

clue.text: … compound starts from any colour you like

indicators.note: starts from means taking the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A chemical compound you can choose in any shade.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the clue for 23 Across but plays no part in the wordplay. Any Colour You Like is a Pink Floyd track.
explanation.definitionFit: An acyl is a group derived from an acid, found in chemical compounds.

clue.text: Besides American players of Star Wars theme

parts.note: the London Symphony Orchestra, LSO, recorded the Star Wars score

explanation.surface: Besides the American musicians who played the Star Wars music.
explanation.definitionFit: Also means in addition, as does besides.

clue.text: Intimidates US and them, having no border, unusually

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd way, so the letters are rearranged
having no means the following piece is taken out of the word them

parts.note: a hem is the border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Us against them, with no boundary, frightens in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' removes HEM from THEM, leaving T; US, AND and T are then rearranged. Us and Them is a Pink Floyd track.
explanation.definitionFit: To daunt is to discourage or frighten someone.

clue.text: Go beyond how speed cameras look to record

parts.note: speed cameras look over the street, abbreviated as OVER ST
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Speed cameras looking out to record drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The cameras look over the street, OVER ST; then EP.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstep is to exceed a limit, as speeders do.
